new_task_1.title: Report publish HTTP failures even when no response object is attached
new_task_1.description: Poetry 1.7.0 hardens publish/upload error handling so an `HTTPError` raised without an attached HTTP response is converted into a user-facing repository connection error instead of failing while formatting the upload exception. Existing detailed formatting for HTTP errors that do include a response remains unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that publish/upload failures surfaced as `HTTPError` still produce a usable user-facing upload error even when the exception has no `response` object attached.

expectation.grounded: When `UploadError` is constructed from an `HTTPError`, it must handle both cases where `error.response` is present and where it is `None`. If a response exists, the message should continue to include the HTTP status code, reason, and response content. If no response exists, the message should fall back to a generic repository connection error instead of dereferencing missing response fields.
expectation.conceptual: Publishing should report HTTP upload failures cleanly even when the underlying client cannot provide a full response object. Users should receive a stable, understandable error instead of an internal exception while Poetry is trying to format the failure.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing `ConnectionError` message. Do not remove detailed status, reason, and content output for `HTTPError` instances that do include a response. Limit the fix to response-less `HTTPError` handling in the publish/upload path.
constraints.conceptual: The change should improve robustness of failure reporting without altering successful uploads or reducing detail for ordinary HTTP failures.

behavior: HTTP upload failures with an attached response continue to render detailed status, reason, and body content in the upload error message.
HTTP upload failures without an attached response now render a generic repository-connection HTTP error message instead of failing during message construction.
ConnectionError-based upload failures continue to produce the existing repository reachability guidance.
acceptance_criteria: When a publish/upload flow raises an `HTTPError` whose response object is available, Poetry should still surface an upload error that includes the response status code, reason, and content.

When a publish/upload flow raises an `HTTPError` with no response object, Poetry should surface a stable upload error indicating an HTTP/repository connection problem rather than crashing with an attribute access failure.
When a publish/upload flow raises a `ConnectionError`, Poetry should keep the existing connection guidance unchanged.

new_task_2.title: Expose fastjsonschema-style diagnostics for invalid Poetry configuration
new_task_2.description: Poetry 1.7.0 replaces the top-level `tool.poetry` schema validator with `fastjsonschema`, changing the validation messages surfaced for invalid configuration. CLI and API flows that report Poetry-schema errors now use fastjsonschema-style wording and path notation for those failures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that invalid `tool.poetry` configuration is validated through the new fastjsonschema-backed validator and that the resulting user-visible diagnostics reflect that validator's error format.

expectation.grounded: Poetry's `validate_object()` flow for `poetry.json` must compile and run the schema with `fastjsonschema` instead of `jsonschema.Draft7Validator`. When that validation fails, the reported Poetry-schema error should surface `JsonSchemaException.message`, which uses fastjsonschema-style wording and `data...` path notation rather than the previous bracketed-path jsonschema messages. These updated diagnostics must be reflected in higher-level validation consumers such as `Factory.validate()`, invalid-project creation errors, and `poetry check` output.
expectation.conceptual: Users should still receive configuration validation failures, but the phrasing and path format of Poetry-schema errors should now match the new validation engine rather than the old jsonschema output.

constraints.grounded: Keep the scope limited to diagnostics emitted from the Poetry-specific schema validation pass. Do not remove additional non-schema validation errors or warnings that are appended by higher-level validation logic. Do not claim behavioral changes for successful configuration validation.
constraints.conceptual: This change should alter how Poetry-schema validation failures are described, not whether valid projects pass validation or whether unrelated custom checks still run.

behavior: Invalid Poetry-schema fields now produce fastjsonschema-formatted error text.
Validation paths for Poetry-schema failures now use `data...` notation rather than the prior bracketed absolute-path formatting.

Higher-level validation surfaces such as `Factory.validate()`, project creation failures, and `poetry check` propagate the updated Poetry-schema diagnostics alongside their existing additional validation output.
acceptance_criteria: When `tool.poetry.source[0].priority` contains an unsupported value, Poetry validation should report a fastjsonschema-style message using `data.source[0].priority` path notation.
When an invalid source entry combines disallowed legacy and new keys, Poetry validation should surface the fastjsonschema disallowed-definition message rather than the previous jsonschema phrasing.

When a required Poetry configuration field such as `description` is missing, higher-level validation output should include the fastjsonschema-style missing-property message while preserving any additional non-schema validation errors reported in the same flow.
